title: What are TypeScript generics
question: What are generics in TypeScript and why are they useful?
realWorldScenario: A `identity<T>(x: T): T` function works for any type — same concept as Java generics for writing reusable, type-safe code.

title: Generic function syntax
question: How do you write a generic function in TypeScript? Show the syntax with type parameter `T`.
searchIntent: how to write generic function typescript
realWorldScenario: A `getFirst<T>(arr: T[]): T | undefined` function works for arrays of any type.

title: Generic constraints with extends
question: How do you constrain a generic type parameter in TypeScript using `extends`?
searchIntent: how to add constraints to typescript generics
realWorldScenario: `<T extends { id: number }>` ensures the generic type has an `id` property, allowing you to access it safely.

title: Built-in generic types
question: What are some commonly used built-in generic types in TypeScript?
realWorldScenario: `Promise<User>` tells TypeScript that the resolved value is a `User` — essential when typing API calls.

title: Generic interfaces
question: How do you define a generic interface in TypeScript?
searchIntent: how to define generic interface typescript
realWorldScenario: `interface ApiResponse<T> { data: T; status: number; message: string }` reusable for any endpoint response type.

title: Utility types: Partial, Required, Pick, Omit
question: What are TypeScript utility types and what do `Partial<T>`, `Required<T>`, `Pick<T,K>`, and `Omit<T,K>` do?
realWorldScenario: `Partial<User>` for update endpoints where not all fields are required; `Omit<User, 'password'>` for public user responses.

title: Generics vs any
question: When should you use generics instead of `any` in TypeScript?
searchIntent: why use generics instead of any typescript
realWorldScenario: `any` disables type checking entirely; generics preserve type information through transformations — use generics to stay type-safe.
